messages:
maria (eng-ml): heads-up: after last night's fp8 rollout we saw a regression in small-batch throughput when per-channel calibration is enabled. p95 token latency up ~18% on dedicated small requests. anyone else seeing this?
kevin (eng-runtime): saw it on canary too. looks correlated with KV cache warmup + per-channel quant mats. I think kernel selection is choosing slower fp8 path for short seqs.
chen (eng-ml): can you paste the perf digests? was this with batching disabled?
sofia (perf): summary from perf-bot:```
Case: small-batch (batches 1-4), seq_len 32
Baseline (int8 per-tensor): p95=42ms, throughput=24 tok/s
FP8/per-tensor: p95=40ms, throughput=26 tok/s
FP8/per-channel: p95=50ms, throughput=21 tok/s
Note: KV hits low for first 10 tokens
```
maria (eng-ml): exact. the weird part: fp8 per-channel is butter for longer batches; regression only for tiny batches with cold KV.
kevin (eng-runtime): hypothesis: per-channel quant layers force a different kernel that materializes quant params per head, and that extra memory op wins at scale but dominates for small microbatches. also KV copy/warmup pokes the same memory bus.
chen (eng-ml): that matches our microbench: per-channel quant step adds a ~0.9ms/attn-head overhead for the first step due to unpack+scale. multiplied by 64 heads becomes noticeable.
sofia (perf): we should consider two levers: 1) runtime kernel routing: prefer per-tensor kernel when batch_size<=4 or KV cold, 2) calibration change: fall back to per-tensor for attention/qkv only. thoughts?
maria (eng-ml): prefer runtime routing. customers expect better quality from per-channel generally; switching cal strategy reduces quality for some heads. but routing is safer.
kevin (eng-runtime): agree. we can add a simple heuristic: if effective_tokens_per_request < 128 OR kv_hit_rate < 0.6 -> choose per-tensor fp8 path. low risk and cheap to implement.
chen (eng-ml): any quality evals showing per-tensor drop is large for our calibration sets? we need to check eval suite for head-level failure modes.
sofia (perf): quick eval on our 2k calibration probes: average ppl delta ~0.02, but some outliers up to 0.5 during math-heavy prompts. outlier count ~0.7% for per-tensor vs per-channel.
maria (eng-ml): that 0.7% is the tricky bit — high business impact for some customers. idea: selective per-channel only for layers flagged by calibration as having >threshold sensitivity. per-layer policy.
kevin (eng-runtime): runtime could read a per-model policy blob produced by the calibrator: e.g., `{"layers":[false,true,true,...], "default":"per-tensor"}` and dispatch kernels accordingly. cheap to check at layer init.
chen (eng-ml): that would be ideal. calibrator needs to emit sensitivity metric and outlier analysis. current calibrator only outputs scale/zero-point per-tensor/channel. we need to extend.
sofia (perf): extending calibrator to compute a simple layer-sensitivity score is straightforward: run N samples, compute output delta between per-tensor and per-channel quant, and rank. small patch.
maria (eng-ml): agree. two action items: 1) kevin/eng-runtime add kernel-routing heuristic + config hook (short-term), 2) chen/eng-ml extend calibrator to emit per-layer sensitivity + recommended kernel (mid-term).
kevin (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR for the heuristic today: will include an opt-in env var and a toggled config. will also add a metric `kernel_choice` to traces so we can see distribution.
chen (eng-ml): I'll prototype calibrator change and run on our 10 calibration corpora. question on outlier handling: do we clip samples or keep them? currently we drop top 1% by L2 before computing sensitivity. should we tighten?
sofia (perf): dropping top 1% helps stability but may hide real rare-but-important failure modes. proposal: keep outliers but tag them; produce both median and 95th sensitivity. use median for recommended kernel but surface 95th in console.
maria (eng-ml): nice. that gives customers visibility. also add an opt in `strict_quality_mode` that forces per-channel if any layer 95th_sensitivity > 0.3.
kevin (eng-runtime): sounds good. I'll also add a runtime flag to force `per-channel-forced-layers` if the model policy asks.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/kernel-routing PR merges -> canary rollout 03:00 UTC tonight.
maria (eng-ml): thanks. last ask: can perf-bot include KV hit-rate correlation in the next digest? would be helpful to validate the heuristic.
perf-bot: noted — will attach kv_hit_rate/time buckets in next run.
kevin (eng-runtime): will add a small flame graph capture and link it in the PR description.
chen (eng-ml): I'll run a quick eval to quantify quality delta on the 0.7% outliers and report back by EOD.
maria (eng-ml): perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin (eng-runtime): quick snippet of the heuristic I plan to land:```json
{"decision": "if effective_tokens < 128 or kv_hit_rate < 0.6 -> per-tensor else per-channel"}
```
maria (eng-ml): posting test checklist here: - canary metrics p95/throughput - kernel_choice distribution - kv_hit_rate buckets - calibrator per-layer sensitivity + 95th - opt-in strict_quality_mode
sofia (perf): I'll own the gating thresholds and rollback criteria. if p95 reg >10% for small-batch after routing change -> rollback.
chen (eng-ml): adding note: for models with many tiny heads (eg 128 heads) threshold needs tuning. we'll run sweep.
maria (eng-ml): ok locking this in. follow-ups in this thread.
